description:
Team UNIX brings together programming, education and life sciences .
We blend technology and education to create an immersive, interactive storytelling experience that brings NASA’s historic abandoned equipment on the Moon and Mars back to life .
Our goal is to inspire the next generation of space enthusiasts .
summary:
Welcome We are UNIX Team.
ECHOES - Beyond The Mission is an interactive digital space museum designed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 .
It addresses the " Abandoned but not Forgotten " challenge by transforming scattered historical space data into an engaging exploration experience .
The Website features dual 2D/3D maps of the Moon and Mars, rich mission cards powered by official NSSDCA archives, an interactive quiz rewarding completion certificates and a rule-based AI guide .
ECHOES makes 60+ years of space history accessible to students and space enthusiasts worldwide .
details: What it does & how it work : ECHOES is an open-access Website that brings historic space exploration to life . It features a dual map system ( Leaflet 2D interactive maps and Three.js 3D globe models ) allowing users to explore exact landing coordinates and hardware left on the Moon and Mars . Users can read detailed mission cards, track historical milestones on a timeline, test their knowledge with a 12-question quiz to earn a verifiable PDF certificate, and query a local rule-based assistant . Benefits & Impact : Makes decades of complex space archives accessible and engaging for school-age enthusiasts and the general public, preserving space history and inspiring the next generation of explorers . Tools & Tech Stack : Built using React / Next.js & Vite, Tailwind CSS for responsive styling, Three.js / React Three Fiber for 3D globe rendering, Leaflet.js for 2D maps .and jsPDF / html2canvas for client-side certificate generation. Hosted globally via Vercel . Creativity & Considerations : Focused on bilingual support ( Arabic & English with RTL/LTR capabilities ), factual accuracy through curated NASA NSSDCA archives and a cinematic space-museum user experience .
